game.summary: Wired §9's fruit into MatchRoom. pedestalSites puts one pedestal on each regular island at its highest-id dock (4). The deal comes from deriveSeed('fruit'), with a test-only pin (PIRATE_SEA_RACE_TEST_FRUITS). stepFruits runs each world tick after the encounters and ruin presence, before the holds and the claim. Protocol v9: F is Buttons.Fruit, plus inspect-fruit / fruit-kit (reply to the inspector only, strict zod), per-client pedestal markers (full or empty, in sight) and the player's own kit, progress and last result in their status. Every sea duel's DuelMachine gets both kits: they are fixed in the frame-0 state and synced in the lobby's kits field, and both clients build the same state from them. Web: fruit panel (F inspects, holding F eats, progress ring, every refusal and interruption reason), HUD kit line, duel HUD kits, arena drawing model from fighterTells (bolts, smoke zones, obscured startup flash, reappearance, threats only for striking moves), pedestal markers on the sea. Ruins P2 items: the panel keydown router skips text fields, a Digit1-6 vs tablet-order test, an exact lockout test, and an open-water test; row 20 is now removed. Docs: architecture 'Fruits in the room', duel.md note, README. Branch table docs/fruit-kits-online-coverage.md: 135 rows (116 tested, 8 equivalent, 11 removed), built by deleting each branch on scratch copies outside the repo. Checks run on the final code: npm ci at the start; typecheck OK; test:unit 1352/1352; test:integration 124/124 in 177 s; build and smoke OK; full Playwright suite 14/14 with the JSON report, which check-report accepts (fruit-duel included).
open_assumptions: The opponent receives the kit in the duel lobby's synced 'kits' field (in the two fighters' views only, from the reservation). There is no separate duel-start message; the integration test checks raw frames.

Casting off while eating ends with the fruit rules' reason 'released'. The panel shows it as 'You cast off' when the player is no longer at a pedestal. A stream that lapses (250 ms) before the room records the drop also ends as 'released'.
While F stays down at the pedestal the player just emptied, the per-tick 'already-eaten' refusal doesn't replace the meal as their last result.
Threat hitboxes are still drawn only under the developer toggle, as before, but only for strikesWithHitbox moves. Bolts, smoke zones, the obscured startup flash and the reappearance are always drawn.

ruins-online row 20: the room's at-sea check in receiveOpenRuin was redundant with the rules, so it was removed. The row is now 'removed' and cites the new open-water test, because deleting that check can't make any test fail.

findings.message: The fruit panel closes on the same tick that the reserved and cast-off interruptions happen, so the page never shows those two reasons. When a grapple lands or the ship casts off, MatchRoom.mirrorObjectives passes no pedestal to mirrorFruit (moored needs !held and a dock). status.pedestal becomes "" on the tick the room records fruitResult 'interrupted:reserved' or 'interrupted:released'. FruitPanel.update (apps/web/src/fruitPanel.ts) then closes the panel because !canInspect(status). fruit-message is the only place resultLine is rendered, so 'A duel interrupted your meal' and 'You cast off: eating stopped' never reach the player. The resultLine cast-off branch (coverage row 63) can only run in unit tests. The arena taking over the screen, or the ship sailing off, makes the cause obvious, so the impact is low. Fix: keep the panel's last message visible after it closes, for example on a HUD line.
findings.requirement: The panel shows why an attempt was refused or interrupted (`taken`, `already-eaten`, `empty`, `reserved`, `disconnected`).

findings.message: Keeping the inspecting F press held down starts eating with no second press. FruitPanel.keydown (apps/web/src/fruitPanel.ts) sets held = true for any KeyF keydown while the panel is open, and it checks event.repeat only on the closed-panel path. Once the fruit-kit reply opens the panel, the browser's auto-repeat keydowns (repeat: true) from the same press turn on Buttons.Fruit, and the fruit, which can't be undone for the match, is eaten about 3.5 s after the first press. This contradicts the unit test's own comment 'The press that inspected does not eat; the next one, held, does.' Neither the test nor Playwright's keyboard.down produces auto-repeat. Fix: ignore repeat keydowns unless F is already held, or ignore F until a keyup follows the inspecting press.
findings.requirement: Holding F for 3 s from the panel eats it, with a progress ring.

findings.message: receiveOpenRuin (apps/server/src/MatchRoom.ts) no longer checks island === null. It casts presenceOf(...).island to number and passes a null island into openRuin, whose OpenRuinRequest type says island: number. Behaviour is correct today only because the pure module checks isIsland at runtime ('invalid-request', no clue, state unchanged) and the clue schema rejects a null clue, which the new open-water test confirms. Still, the cast hides a type mismatch across the module boundary, and receiveAnswerRuin in the same file keeps an explicit null branch. A typed guard, or a row marked tested instead of 'removed', would have met the carried item without the cast.
findings.requirement: a room-level test shows that an open-ruin from open water sends no clue. Replace the `equivalent` row in `docs/ruins-online-coverage.md` with it.

findings.message: The raw-message hidden-information test in tests/integration/fruits.test.ts ("sends a pedestal's kit only to the player moored there who inspects it ...") only reads frames sent after the marks it takes at line 357. By then playersAt() has already joined the players, placed their ships in sight of Palm Key and Mist Cay, and started the match through the lobby. So the first sync of each player's pedestal markers and own status happens before any frame is recorded. For the far player, pedestal-3's marker never changes afterwards, so none of its encoding is ever checked. No integration test scans frames from join (framesSince(0)) for kit names. If the deal leaked into the first sync (a kit field on PedestalMarkerSchema, or in another player's status), no test would fail. Today's schema carries no kit, so this is a gap in the test, not a defect.
findings.requirement: no message to any other player names a pedestal's kit

findings.message: No test shows that a duel fought after a defeat starts with the eater's kit. The test 'refuses a fed player's further attempts and an empty pedestal, and keeps the kit through a lost duel' (tests/integration/fruits.test.ts:274) checks only the status field fruitView().kit === 'ember' after the respawn. It never grapples again to check seaDuelDiagnostics(...).kits or the lobby's kits in a later duel. The only duel-kit test (line 314) checks the eater's first duel.
findings.requirement: The eaten kit replaces the player's two specials (U, I) in every sea duel for the rest of the match, including after a defeat.

inputs.decisions:
# Decisions: fruit-kits-online

From the operator session of 2026-09-25. The operator asked the assistant to keep launching the queued slices on the 10-minute loop. The assistant settled the choices below, and they're recorded in `operator-logs/decisions-overnight.md` (#51).

## Decisions

- The pure fruits and duel modules on `main` are used through their exports and aren't owned. The room passes `createFruitState` a fruit seed derived from the master secret (`deriveSeed('fruit')`).
- There's one pedestal per regular island, at the island's highest-id dock (`pedestalSites`, in `apps/server/src`). That gives 4 sites in the slice: 2 Ember and 2 Smoke.
- F inspects a pedestal, and holding F for 3 s eats it. The panel shows the kit name, its specials, its §9 description and every refusal or interruption reason. F doesn't clash with E, R, J, U or I.
- Every sea duel starts with both players' kits, fixed in the initial duel state, so the per-frame hash covers them. A player's kit is private until a duel starts.
- The arena draws bolts, smoke screens, the obscured fighter's startup flash and the feint's reappearance from `fighterTells`. Threat hitboxes are drawn only for `strikesWithHitbox` moves.
- The new browser scenario is `fruit-duel`. The other scenarios keep Duelist players and behave as before.
- The four P2 notes from `ruins-online`'s approving reviews are folded in. One of them is a bug: R typed in a text field opens a ruin.
- The committed branch → test table (`docs/fruit-kits-online-coverage.md`) is required from the start.

## Assumptions

- Everything in `features/match-online/`, `features/ruins-online/` and their fixes stands.
- Tests pin the fruit deal with a test-only setting, like the ruins and sources.

## Deferred

- `intel-online` (rumors, journal, reveals UI) and then `economy-online` (shops, tonics, supply caches).

concerns.message: The design says the pedestal at an island's highest-id dock 'differs from the rubbing source's dock'. In the slice that isn't true. The slice preset has sourcesPerIsland = 2, every slice island has exactly 2 docks, and `sourceSites` places source slot j at docks[j % docks.length]. So both docks of every island hold a source, and each pedestal shares its dock with source-i-1. The pedestals are separate objects from the sources, as §9 asks, but they don't have their own locations.
concerns.consequence: A worker who writes the `pedestalSites` unit test as 'pedestal dock is not a source dock' gets a test that can never pass. They may then 'fix' the site rule and break the settled decision, or report blocked. The test should assert 4 distinct docks, one per island, each the island's highest-id dock. The HUD at that dock has to show the E (collect) and F (inspect fruit) prompts together, and the browser test must expect both.

concerns.message: 'Tests pin the fruit deal with a test-only setting' has no matching pure operation. `createFruitState(sites, seed, preset)` only shuffles from a seed. There's no assignment constructor like the ledger's `createLedgerFromAssignment`.
concerns.consequence: The worker may wrongly report `blocked` for a missing pure operation. Two routes need no pure change: build a literal `FruitState` (the types are exported, and `checkFruitState` validates it), or search derived seeds (`fruit:<n>`) the way the pinned ruins search `ruins:<n>`. Either way, the test setting must be refused outside test mode, like the other test settings.

concerns.message: The plan says both clients get the kits in 'the duel start message', but there is no such message. Clients build the initial duel state from the sea duel's lobby schema (`createDuelState(defaultDuelConfig, { seed: lobby.seed })` in `apps/web/src/duelClient.ts:152` and `:208`, and the same pattern in test-tools' HeadlessClient). The lobby is created, and added to both fighters' views, when the grapple lands (`openSeaDuel`), not when the fight starts. Every place that builds a duel state needs the kits: `DuelMachine`'s constructor, the web session, the HUD fallback, the headless fighter, and the reconnect snapshot.
concerns.consequence: If any one of these still defaults to the Duelist mirror, the per-frame hash mismatches on every frame of an Ember or Smoke duel (acceptance #4 fails), or the HUD shows the wrong move names. Also, if the kits go into the lobby at reservation, the opponent learns them even when the encounter is later cancelled before the fight. Say which point counts as 'duel start' in the hidden-information test.

concerns.message: The `reserved` flag passed to `stepFruits` has to reflect this tick's encounter results. Sea duels, and the kits they carry, are created inside `stepEncounters` via `openSeaDuel`. The `held` set is computed at the start of `advance()`, before encounters run.
concerns.consequence: If the room fills `reserved` from `held`, a player whose 3 s channel completes on the same tick they're grappled eats the fruit after their duel was already created with the Duelist kit. They then fight that duel with the wrong kit, which breaks 'the eaten kit is used in every sea duel'. Compute `reserved` from the encounter or ledger state after `stepEncounters`.

concerns.message: The tap-versus-hold input is unspecified. If F is a latched world button like E and J (`keyboard.ts` LATCHED), the tap that opens the panel also reaches the server as a held tick. That produces `eat-started`, then `eat-interrupted`/`released` on the next tick. Also, the plan's list of panel reasons leaves out `released`, `moved`, `gap` and `left`, all of which the pure step emits. `eat-refused` repeats on every held tick.
concerns.consequence: The panel shows 'interrupted: released' right after it opens, or an unhandled reason. Forwarding every per-tick refusal as its own message floods the client at 20 Hz and can trip rate or size caps. Send changes only, and map every `FruitInterruptReason` and `FruitRefusalReason` to text.

concerns.message: `stepFruits` throws a `RangeError` for an unknown pedestal id or a duplicate player, and any throw inside `worldTick` calls `fault()`, which aborts the match (§12).
concerns.consequence: A bug in the room's dock-to-pedestal mapping, such as passing a dock id or a pedestal for an island without one, ends every live match instead of just failing an eat. Map dock → pedestal id with an explicit lookup that returns null otherwise, and unit-test it.

concerns.message: Workload and time limits. The branch table requires deleting each branch in parallel batches, and several of those runs must go through the integration or browser suites. Integration tests run in real time: 3 s eats, grapple countdowns, and a roughly 500-frame lost duel for 'kit survives defeat'. The browser suite uses fixed webServer ports, and the machine is shared. On top of that come the 4 carried ruins items and a new e2e scenario, all within a 3-hour worker deadline.
concerns.consequence: The worker is likely to run out of time on the branch table or hit port collisions when batching browser-level deletions. That leaves `untested` rows or a late `blocked`. Give each scratch copy its own port or run browser mutations one at a time, record the current integration duration first, and finish the table before polishing the arena drawing.

challenge.simpler_alternative: Treat F exactly like E: a world-input button bit, held and repeated through the existing input gate. Don't add a separate inspect request/response message. The first F press while moored at a pedestal's dock both starts the channel and makes the server send that player the pedestal's inspection once per mooring. The panel opens on that reply and shows the progress ring from the same channel; holding for 3 s eats, and letting go interrupts. This keeps every settled rule: F opens the panel, holding F for 3 s eats, and only the player at the dock who pressed F sees the kit. It also drops a new zod message, its rate limiter, the extra hidden-information path and the client-side tap-versus-hold logic.
challenge.cheap_experiment: Run a scratch tsx one-liner that prints `sourceSites(seaMap)` next to `islandDocks(seaMap, i)` and the proposed highest-id dock for each island. It will show whether every slice dock already holds a source, so every pedestal would share a dock with source-i-1. If so, the operator should confirm that's acceptable (§9 says pedestals are 'distinct from rubbing sources') before the worker writes `pedestalSites` and its unit test. In the same script, build a literal `FruitState` with a pinned Ember/Smoke deal and run it through `checkFruitState` and one `stepFruits` tick. That confirms the test-only pinned deal works without a pure-module change.

game.task:
# Task: game

## Goal

Make fruit powers part of the race (§9). Four fruit pedestals, two Ember and two Smoke, sit at island docks. Moored at a pedestal's dock, a captain can inspect its kit: the two specials and what they're good for. Holding **F** for 3 s eats the fruit, and releasing F, casting off, a grapple, a disconnect or someone else finishing first interrupts it. The eaten kit replaces the player's two specials (U, I) in every sea duel for the rest of the match, including after a defeat. The arena draws the Ember and Smoke moves: flame bolts, the rising flare, the feint's reappearance and the smoke screen with its obscured fighters. Both players can read what's happening. The pure rules are on `main` (`packages/simulation/src/fruits`, `docs/fruits.md`; the kits in `packages/simulation/src/duel`, `docs/fruit-kits.md`). This feature wires them in.

## Context

- Read `docs/spec.md` §9 (all of it), §6 (duels at sea), §12 (disconnects) and §16 (hidden information).
- Read `docs/fruits.md` (`createFruitState`, `stepFruits`, `kitOf`, `inspectPedestal`, the events, contests by id), `docs/fruit-kits.md` (the kit data, `createDuelState(config, { kits })`, the step changes, and "What the renderer must show": `fighterTells`, `strikesWithHitbox`), `docs/duel.md` (the netcode, and a duel inside the match room), `docs/architecture.md` (the room, the master secret and per-system seeds, the ruins wiring as a model) and `apps/server/src/objectives.ts` (`sourceSites`, `islandDocks`).
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration`, `npm run build` and `npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts`.
- **This machine is shared by several runs. Never stop processes by name pattern (`pkill -f`, `killall`, and so on). Stop only the PIDs you started.**

## Constraints

- Owned paths as in `policy.json`. The pure modules and their content aren't owned: use them through their exports, and report `blocked` naming the gap if a change is truly needed.
- Server authoritative, zod-validated messages, protocol version bump. One Phaser game per page, canvas renderer for the match game (decision #43).
- Tests drive input like players do.
- Hidden information: the deal (which pedestal holds which kit) is revealed only to a player moored at that pedestal's dock who inspects it. Other players see a pedestal's marker (full or empty) only when it's in sight. A player's kit is private until a duel starts; then both duelists see both kits, because the arena shows the moves.
- Duel netcode: the kits must be fixed in the duel's initial state on both clients and the server (the per-frame hash covers them), so a kit never desyncs a duel.

## Design (settled)

- **Sites:** one pedestal per regular island at that island's docks, chosen in the server like `sourceSites`: the island's highest-id dock, so it differs from the rubbing source's dock whenever the island has more than one. That gives 4 sites in the slice, which is what `createFruitState` needs. A pure function `pedestalSites(map)` in `apps/server/src`, unit-tested.
- **Seed:** the fruit deal uses its own seed derived from the master secret (`deriveSeed('fruit')`), never the match code or another system's seed.
- **Inspect and eat:** moored at a pedestal's dock, the HUD shows "F: inspect fruit" on a full pedestal. Pressing F opens a small panel with the kit name, its two specials and its §9 description from `kitDescriptions`. Holding F for 3 s from the panel eats it, with a progress ring. The panel shows why an attempt was refused or interrupted (`taken`, `already-eaten`, `empty`, `reserved`, `disconnected`). Once fed, the HUD shows the kit ("Ember: U flame bolt, I rising flare"). F doesn't clash with E (collect), R (ruin) or J (grapple), and the ruin panel's key-typing rules apply to this panel too.
- **Into duels:** the room creates every sea duel with `kits: [kitOf(a), kitOf(b)]`. Both clients receive the kits in the duel start message and build the same initial state. `restoreDuel` and the per-frame hashes cover them.
- **Arena drawing:** the arena scene draws, from `fighterTells`, each fighter's bolt as a moving sprite, the smoke screen as a translucent zone, a generic startup flash for an obscured fighter, the feint's reappearance, and threat hitboxes only for `strikesWithHitbox` moves. The arena HUD shows each fighter's kit and the U and I move names.
- **Tick order:** fruits step in the world tick after encounters and before claims, like the ruins' presence. A duel reservation interrupts eating (the pure rules do this when the room passes `reserved`).

## Goal

Make fruit powers part of the race (§9). Four fruit pedestals, two Ember and two Smoke, sit at island docks. Moored at a pedestal's dock, a captain can inspect its kit: the two specials and what they're good for. Holding **F** for 3 s eats the fruit, and releasing F, casting off, a grapple, a disconnect or someone else finishing first interrupts it. The eaten kit replaces the player's two specials (U, I) in every sea duel for the rest of the match, including after a defeat. The arena draws the Ember and Smoke moves: flame bolts, the rising flare, the feint's reappearance and the smoke screen with its obscured fighters. Both players can read what's happening. The pure rules are on `main` (`packages/simulation/src/fruits`, `docs/fruits.md`; the kits in `packages/simulation/src/duel`, `docs/fruit-kits.md`). This feature wires them in.

scenarios.description: One browser creates a private match from the landing page; the HUD shows the code, the protocol version, one player and a connected status.
Two browsers join the same private match with their ships in sight of each other; one sails with the keyboard and the other browser's view shows that ship at the new server-authoritative position.
A browser sails its ship around a shoal to an island dock with the keyboard and docks there; the HUD shows the dock and the ship stops at it.
Two browsers in one match with their ships out of sight of each other: neither view lists or draws the other ship until one sails within the sight radius, and it disappears again when it sails away.

One browser opens a practice duel against the dummy, lands a jab and then a keyboard throw (J then K a frame apart); the dummy's health bar and the HUD drop by the move data's damage, and hitboxes can be shown.

Two browsers: one creates a duel, the other joins by its code; after the countdown the first lands a strike on the second, and both views show the same authoritative health, round clock and result, with the connection line showing input delay and corrections.

Two browsers in one match are placed within grapple range; the host sails at the guest and presses J; both see the grapple telegraph, then a three-second countdown and the arena; the duel is decided; the winner returns to the sea with protection shown, and the loser sees a respawn countdown and then their ship at a dock.

Two browsers moored at different islands each hold E and collect a different rubbing type; the host grapples the guest at sea, wins the duel by tapping attack keys, and picks the guest's type within five seconds; the host's HUD shows both types and more gold, the guest's shows the loss.

Two browsers: the host starts a private match from the lobby, both see the ready countdown and the match timer; the host collects both rubbing types, sees the full-set reveal and the route, sails to the final island's claim tile and holds E for ten seconds; both browsers show the results with the host as the winner.

Two browsers start a private match from the lobby with test-only short timings; nobody claims; the timer runs out; both browsers show the results with the no-winner deadline headline, and the route compass is shown inactive while no route is known.

One browser moored at an island opens its ruin with R and reads the clue from the page; the test derives the answer from the displayed clue only, submits it, sees '+40 gold' and the island unlocked, then holds E to collect the rubbing.

One browser moors at a pedestal's dock, presses F, reads the kit name from the panel, holds F for three seconds and sees its HUD show Ember; it grapples the second browser at sea, casts the flame bolt (U) in the arena, both browsers see the bolt drawn, and the second browser's health bar drops by the bolt's damage.
